The build makes /books/ pages from this file. intro_html and end_html go at the start and end of the book. cut_headings removes recurring newsletter sections by heading; cut_paragraphs removes matching paragraphs; skip_chapters leaves stories out; draft: true keeps a book off the books and series pages.

books.title: Cycling to the Sahara
books.subtitle: 1,279 miles from London to the desert, by bike, boat and (whisper it) train
books.rights: © David Charles 2012, 2026. Free to read and share.
books.description: In spring 2012 David Charles set off from his front door in London to cycle to the Sahara. Things did not go entirely to plan. Twenty-eight dispatches from the road: French pizza, Marseille ferries, killer guard dogs, Matmata moped men, Ksar Ghilane in the rain, Tunisia a year after its revolution, and an awful lot of couscous.
books.intro_html:
In February 2012 I worked out that it is 1,279 miles from my house in London to the Saharan desert. Not far, eh? So I decided to cycle there.

This book collects the dispatches I wrote along the way, as I wrote them at the time, from the Newhaven ferry to a sand dune in southern Tunisia and back to Tunis in the turbulent spring after the revolution. They were first published on my blog, davidcharles.info. I have only tidied them up a little: some photographs from that era have been lost, and links that no longer work have been left out.

There are twenty-eight chapters. You can read them in order, as a journey, or dip in wherever the road looks interesting.
books.end_html:
Thank you for riding along.

The story didn’t end in Tunis. Four years later I set off again, this time cycling towards Syria along the routes of migration, and later I spent many summers riding with Thighs of Steel. You can read all of it, free, at davidcharles.info/series.

Every Friday I send a short story about adventure, nature and being human to readers of my newsletter. If you enjoyed this book, I’d love you to join them: davidcharles.substack.com.

This book is free to read and share. If you’d like to give something back, the best thing you can do is tell a friend about it.

books.title: Cycling towards Syria
books.subtitle: London to Vienna by bike in 2016, following the routes of migration
books.description: In May 2016 David Charles set off from London to cycle 3,000 miles along the routes people were taking into Europe, collecting stories from refugees, volunteers and officials on the way: Calais and Grande-Synthe, the Belgian asylum system, Germany’s welcome and its limits, and a refugee camp in Vienna.
books.intro_html:
In spring 2016, as more than a million people crossed into Europe seeking safety, David Charles set out from London on his bicycle. His plan was to follow the routes of migration in reverse, towards Syria, listening to the people he met: refugees, volunteers, officials and neighbours.

These are the dispatches he wrote along the way, first published on his blog and newsletter, from the camps of Calais to a refugee centre in Vienna. They are presented as they were written at the time, with a little tidying.
books.end_html:
All of David’s stories, including the other long rides, are free to read at davidcharles.info/series.

David writes short stories about adventure, nature and being human for readers of his newsletter. To join them, visit davidcharles.substack.com.

This book is free to read and share. If you enjoyed it, the best thing you can do is tell a friend.

books.title: Cycling Round Britain (Twice)
books.subtitle: 4,110 miles in 2011, and the long way round again in the 2020s
books.description: Two journeys round the coast of Britain, a decade apart: a solo 4,110-mile ride in 2011, and a slower, stage-by-stage return after lockdown. Tents, rainstorms, cheese sandwiches, ghosts, and what changes when you do the same thing twice.
books.intro_html:
In 2011 David Charles cycled 4,110 miles around the coast of Britain. Nine years later, as lockdown lifted, he set off to do it again, this time in stages, and with a very different view of the country and of himself.

This book gathers his blog posts and newsletter stories from both journeys, as they were first published. The story of the 2011 ride is told in full in his book Life to the Lees.
books.end_html:
All of David’s stories, including the other long rides, are free to read at davidcharles.info/series.

David writes short stories about adventure, nature and being human for readers of his newsletter. To join them, visit davidcharles.substack.com.

This book is free to read and share. If you enjoyed it, the best thing you can do is tell a friend.

books.title: Thighs of Steel
books.subtitle: Riding in solidarity with people on the move, 2017–2025
books.description: Thighs of Steel was a relay bike ride from London (and later Glasgow) to Athens, raising over £760,000 for projects run by and for refugees. David Charles rode with it, organised it and wrote about it for eight summers. These are his stories: the riders, the roads, the people on the move, and what it means to build a community on wheels.
books.intro_html:
Thighs of Steel was a relay bike ride across Europe, from London and later Glasgow to Athens, raising money for projects run by refugees for refugees. Over its lifetime the riders raised more than £760,000.

David Charles first joined the ride in 2018, then became part of the core team that ran it. This book collects what he wrote about it in his blog and his weekly newsletter, from the first mention in 2017 to the goodbye in 2025. Other newsletter news from the same weeks has been left out.
books.end_html:
All of David’s stories, including the other long rides, are free to read at davidcharles.info/series.

David writes short stories about adventure, nature and being human for readers of his newsletter. To join them, visit davidcharles.substack.com.

This book is free to read and share. If you enjoyed it, the best thing you can do is tell a friend.
